title: Hotel Key Cards — VingCard / Saflok / Salto / ONITY / MIFARE Plus EV2 / DESFire EV3 Procurement Guide
summary: The right hotel key card is determined by lock compatibility first, then chip family, then encoding workflow. And only then by material or finish. This page helps procurement teams work through those decisions in the right order across ASSA ABLOY VingCard / Mobile Access, dormakaba Saflok / Confidant, Salto SVN / KS, ONITY HT / Advance, MIWA Lock, Häfele Dialock, Be-Tech and Kaba estates — with direct links to compatibility pages, chip comparison tools and sample planning guides.
heroPoints: Match the chip family to the lock estate before specifying artwork or premium finishes.
Understand encoding workflow (pre-encoded, blank-issued or PMS-linked) before ordering.
Fast sampling starts from a current card reference or lock model, not a generic PVC spec.
imageAlt: Stack of branded hotel RFID key cards ready for encoding

brief.label: Audience
items: Hotels and serviced apartments replacing or refreshing their room-key program.
Resorts evaluating eco, wood or premium card materials alongside their standard stock.
Procurement teams building a compatibility-first sample plan before requesting pricing.
Multi-property groups standardising chip family and encoding across a lock estate.

brief.label: Decision sequence
items: Lock platform and chip family: MIFARE Classic, MIFARE Plus or DESFire EV3.
Encoding workflow: pre-encoded by supplier, blank cards issued at front desk, or PMS-linked.
Material path: standard PVC, eco PLA, wood or specialty card stock.
Magstripe co-layer requirement for legacy readers still in the property.

Häfele Dialock + Tag-it HF-I + LE / FT / FH / DT — MIFARE Classic + DESFire EV2/EV3 across European boutique and serviced-apartment estates.
Be-Tech eGuard / B-Lite / B-Free + Kaba Confidant + Kaba Atlas — MIFARE Classic / Plus EV2 + Kaba 2533 protocol on legacy estates.

items: Oracle OPERA Cloud / OPERA 5 PMS + OPERA Vendor Interface (OVI) for guest-key issue, encoder driver via OPERA OVI / OWS.

Sample-brief input list: PMS name + version, encoder model (e.g. ASSA ABLOY VingCard Allure encoder, dormakaba Saflok 5750), encoder driver software version, MIFARE chip family + sector layout, online/standalone door mix, mobile-key plan.

brief.label: Card-body materials — environmental + finish profile
items: Standard PVC ID-1 0.76 mm — lowest cost, full CMYK + spot UV + foil + metallic ink + serial-number marking.
Eco PLA bio-resin — biodegradable plant-derived alternative; passes EU 2022/2380 ESPR draft criteria for hospitality giveaway items.
Wood-veneer (FSC-certified bamboo / cherry / walnut) — laser-engraved branding for boutique and luxury properties.
Composite PET-G / PVC blend — increased flex tolerance for resorts with poolside and beach-bag use cases.
Recycled rPVC (50–100 % post-consumer) — sustainability-procurement option matching Green Key / EarthCheck / LEED criteria.
Metal hybrid (stainless / brass with HF inlay window) — luxury VIP suite credential at small volumes (≤1000 / property).

brief.label: Encoding lifecycle and key-rotation policy
items: Per-stay encoding: card written at check-in, expires at check-out — standard for transient hotels.
Permanent / staff: programmer-card based MIFARE Plus EV2 with role-based access to back-of-house, housekeeping, F&B and engineering doors.
Master / emergency: generated and audited by GM / security manager; physical custody log and quarterly rotation per AHLA / brand-standard policy.
Key rotation: master keys rotated every 90 days, application keys re-derived per dormakaba / ASSA ABLOY brand standards; site-key change after security incident.
PCI-DSS SAQ-A scope avoidance: keep PMS payment tokenisation separate from key-encoding workflow — encoder drivers do not handle card payments.

brief.label: Mobile-key complement — BLE / NFC alongside plastic
items: ASSA ABLOY Mobile Access — BLE / NFC over Hospitality Mobile Access SDK, integrated with Marriott Bonvoy, Hilton Honors, IHG One Rewards.
Salto JustIN Mobile + Salto KS Cloud — BLE per-stay key for mid-scale and lifestyle brands, no app-download required for one-time guests.
dormakaba Saflok Mobile Access + LENS — Hyatt + Wyndham + Choice Hotels deployments using Saflok Messenger online infrastructure.
ONITY DirectKey + Trillium ZigBee online — DoubleTree, Hampton, Embassy Suites + select Hilton.
Apple Wallet hotel keys — Hyatt + Hilton + Marriott pilot deployments; plastic remains primary for guests without compatible iPhone / iOS or for sub-properties on legacy lock firmware.

brief.label: Brand-standard and compliance considerations
items: Marriott Bonvoy: Mobile Access mandatory across full-service and select-service brands by 2025; lock-firmware refresh cycle synchronised across portfolio.
Hilton Honors: Digital Key (BLE) standard at 80 %+ US owned + managed properties; plastic-card requirement at properties with non-converted lock firmware.
IHG One Rewards: IHG Mobile Key on Salto KS at boutique brands (Kimpton, Hotel Indigo, voco) + ASSA ABLOY at Holiday Inn, Crowne Plaza.
AHLA brand-standard book: master-key rotation, lost-card replacement, audit log retention 1–3 years per brand.
GDPR / CCPA: cardholder data does not enter lock estate; encoder log retention typically 90 days standalone, longer when synchronised to PMS.
EU 2022/2380 ESPR (draft): hospitality giveaway items including key cards face material-disclosure obligations from 2027 — eco PLA / FSC wood paths align.

brief.label: Anti-cloning + lost-card lifecycle
items: MIFARE Classic 1K Crypto-1 broken academically since 2008 — recommended for replacement during lock-platform refresh.
MIFARE DESFire EV3 + MIFARE Plus EV2 SL3: AES-128 mutual authentication, no public crack as of 2026.
Lost-card hot-list: synchronised across online doors via gateway; standalone doors invalidate at next master-key recurrence.
Re-issue rate: industry benchmark 8–12 % of guest cards per stay (lost / damaged / missed-return).
Disposal: bulk MIFARE Classic populations cross-shredded with chip-destroy step to satisfy ISO 27001 A.8.10.

sections.title: Pain points procurement teams face with hotel key card suppliers
sections.intro: Most hotel key card failures happen before a single card is printed. The root cause is almost always a compatibility decision that was skipped or deferred until after samples arrived.

items.label: DESFire EV3 + Plus EV2 SL3 baseline

bullets: Cards encoded to the wrong sector layout arrive on-site and fail at the lock. Resampling delays the opening.
Suppliers quote on PVC but can't confirm MIFARE Plus EV2 chip availability at volume, stalling approval.
Artwork approval cycles run in parallel with compatibility testing, causing expensive reprints when the chip changes.
Magstripe co-layer is omitted from the brief because it 'probably won't be needed', then properties with legacy readers can't issue.
Multi-property rollouts discover that each lock platform requires a different chip, fragmenting the order across three suppliers.

before: Property opens RFP with branded card artwork specification before lock-estate audit.
Supplier quotes on PVC stock and assumes 'standard MIFARE' — chip family unconfirmed.
Sample arrives with MIFARE Classic; lock estate is actually MIFARE Plus EV2 SL3 — read fails.
Resampling cycle adds 14–21 days; artwork already approved must be reprinted on correct chip body.
Multi-property programme fragments across 3 suppliers per lock platform — pricing and SKU sprawl.
Mobile-key roadmap deferred because lock firmware version not aligned with mobile-access requirements.
after: Property submits current card reference or lock model + photo first; chip family confirmed in 1 working day.
Sector layout, encoder driver and PMS encoder model agreed under standard NDA before printing begins.
Sample produced on correct chip family + sector layout — first-round read at lock validated 90 %+.
Artwork approved in parallel after compatibility lock-in — no reprint risk on chip mismatch.
Multi-property programme consolidates to single chip family where lock firmware supports — one supplier, one SKU per material variant.
Mobile-access roadmap surfaced during compatibility audit — plastic + BLE plan agreed up-front.

sections.title: How Proud Tek solves hotel key card compatibility
sections.intro: Proud Tek's hotel key card process starts with the lock estate and encoder setup, not with artwork. That sequence eliminates the most common resampling causes.
bullets: Chip matching by lock platform: we map MIFARE Classic, MIFARE Plus EV1/EV2 and DESFire EV3 to the property's confirmed lock and encoder before any card goes into production.
Pre-encoding or blank-card options: cards can ship pre-encoded with a fixed sector layout, or blank for front-desk encoding. The workflow is agreed before printing.
Magstripe co-layer on request: dual-interface cards for properties with mixed reader estates are a standard catalogue item, not a custom project.
Sample turnaround in 7–10 working days: a reference card or lock model photo is enough to begin; full artwork is not required to start the compatibility check.
Multi-property chip standardisation: we can consolidate a single chip family across a mixed lock estate where the lock firmware supports a compatible migration.

sections.title: Chip family comparison for hotel locks
sections.intro: The three main chip families each carry a different tradeoff between legacy compatibility, upgrade complexity and security profile.

rows: MIFARE Classic 1K / 4K
Older VingCard, ONITY, Saflok estates
Widest installed base, lowest resampling risk on legacy estates
Security limitations; migration pressure growing in 2024–2026
MIFARE Plus EV1 / EV2
Mid-generation locks supporting security-level upgrade
Backward-compatible with Classic while supporting AES-128 in SL3
Requires lock and encoder firmware to support the target security level
DESFire EV3
New-build or fully upgraded lock estates
Strongest encryption, multi-application support, mutual authentication
Not backward-compatible; requires confirmed lock and encoder support before ordering

timeline.title: Hotel key-card procurement and rollout — week-by-week

items.text: Walk every floor, log lock brand + model + firmware version (VingCard Signature RFID vs Allure vs Classic; Saflok Quantum vs Confidant; Salto SVN vs KS; ONITY HT22i vs Advance vs DirectKey). Capture front-desk encoder model + driver version. Send Proud Tek a current guest-card reference plus a lock photo for chip-family confirmation.
items.label: Week 1 — Lock-estate audit + reference-card capture

items.text: Confirm chip family per lock platform. Sign NDA for sector-layout / key-block disclosure on pre-encoded path; or confirm blank-card path with on-site encoder. Decide magstripe co-layer requirement based on legacy reader survey (parking, lockers, gym, F&B POS).
items.label: Week 2 — Chip-family lock-in and sector-layout NDA

items.text: Standard PVC vs eco PLA vs FSC wood vs metal hybrid. Confirm CMYK / spot UV / foil / metallic-ink artwork constraints. Lead-time impact: standard PVC same-day; PLA + 2 days; wood-veneer + 5–7 days; metal hybrid + 14 days.
items.label: Week 3 — Material and finish selection

items.text: Produce 50–100 sample cards on confirmed chip + sector layout. Validate read at one room door + one elevator + one online door + one standalone door + (if applicable) one parking gate / gym / F&B reader. Sign-off triggers full production.
items.label: Week 4 — Compatibility sample at 50–100 cards

items.text: Brand-standard artwork sign-off in parallel. Production wave 1 covers initial inventory (typically 6–8 months of stay-volume). Pre-encoded cards include facility code + lock-platform key block; blank cards ship without encoded data.
items.label: Week 5–6 — Artwork proofing and full production

items.text: Air or sea freight per opening timeline; Incoterms typically DAP front-desk receiving. Receiving-side QC: visual inspection + 5 % batch read-test + serialised audit-log capture for property records.
items.label: Week 7–8 — Despatch + on-site receiving

items.text: Property tracks per-stay re-issue rate (8–12 % industry benchmark); orders re-stock at 60-day inventory threshold. Master-key rotation begins at 90 days per AHLA / brand-standard policy.
items.label: Month 3 — Re-stock cycle and lost-card pipeline

items.text: Programme references draw from hospitality, luxury-brands, education, healthcare and brand-protection estates, with periodic compliance reviews, refresh-cycle planning and supplier-onboarding gates customised per vertical. annual brand-standard audit with lock-firmware refresh; semi-annual chip-family review for lock-platform changes; eco-material adoption review against Green Key / EarthCheck / LEED criteria; mobile-access (Apple Wallet / BLE) rollout for properties on compatible firmware.
items.label: Quarter 2 onward — Operate, audit and refresh on annual cycle

faq.question: How do I know which chip my hotel locks use?
faq.answer: The fastest method is to send a photo of your current guest card or the lock brand and model. Most lock brands map cleanly to one or two chip families. We can confirm compatibility within one working day in most cases.

faq.question: Can I order cards without providing key data?
faq.answer: Yes, if you choose blank cards for front-desk encoding. Pre-encoded cards require the sector layout and key data, shared under a standard NDA. Most properties with existing encoder setups prefer the blank-card route.

faq.question: Do hotel key cards need a magstripe co-layer?
faq.answer: Only if your property has magnetic-stripe readers still in service. Typically on older parking barriers, gym lockers or legacy room locks. Dual-interface cards with both RFID and magstripe are a standard catalogue option.

faq.question: How long does hotel key card sampling take?
faq.answer: Standard compatibility samples take 7–10 working days from confirmed chip and format. Artwork proofs add 2–3 working days. Providing a current card reference or lock model on first contact usually shortens this to the lower end of the range.

faq.question: Can I get eco or wood hotel key cards in MIFARE Plus?
faq.answer: Yes. Eco PLA and wood-veneer card constructions are available with MIFARE Classic, MIFARE Plus EV2 and DESFire EV3 inlays. Lead times for specialty materials are slightly longer than standard PVC.

faq.question: What is the minimum order quantity for hotel key cards?
faq.answer: Sample quantities start from 50–100 cards depending on the construction. Full production orders typically start from 500 cards for standard PVC and 200–300 for premium or eco materials. Contact the team for quantity-specific pricing.

faq.question: What if my property uses multiple lock brands?
faq.answer: Multi-brand estates are common and usually require a compatibility review across all lock platforms before a single chip family is confirmed. In some cases a dual-application or MIFARE Plus migration strategy can reduce the number of card SKUs in circulation.
